full_judgment:
7. Mr Sarforaj Meah, Advocate along with Mr Md Azahar Ullah Bhuiyan, Advocate and Mr Lokman Hossain, Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioner, has taken me through the judgments of both the Courts, plaint, written statement and the evidence of the parties and submitted that the judgment of the Appellate Court is not a proper judgment al reversal as the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the trial Court arrived at on proper consideration of the materials on record. The learned Advocate at the very outset submitted that the Exhibit 2 is a void document and also drawn my attention to the findings of the trial Court: 

 11. Ms Rebeka Sultana along with Ms. Farzia Karim the learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, has candidly supported the judgment of the Appellate Court and submitted that the Appellate Court having regard to the provisions of Order XII rule 31 has dearly reversed the finding of the trial Court and accordingly, recorded findings and having been satisfied upon discussion of the materials on record has decreed the suit in all counts and thereby, the appellate Court committed no error of law which calls for no interference by this Court and that the judgment of the Appellate Court is a proper judgment of reversal. 

 16. In view of the above, the kabala dated 17-11-1972 having been registered in violation of section 28 of the Registration Act is nothing but a void deed, rather fraud was practiced under the Registration Act and as a result, the plaintiff is not entitled to the decree. I have also perused the decisions cited above and I am of the view that the submissions made by the teamed Advocate of the defendant-petitioner find support in the aforesaid decisions and also I am of the view that the submissions of the teamed Advocate have sufficient substance that the Appellate Court failed to reverse the findings of the trial Court on material points as to maintainability of the suit and also as to status of the Exhibit 2 the kabala dated 17-11-1972 and, as such, it reveals that the judgment of the Appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal as the Appellate Court has failed to reverse the specific findings of the trial Court passed on proper appreciation of the materials on record.
